compiled_state.description:
## Context

`sweep (windows)` in `.github/workflows/test.yml` is an advisory job (`continue-on-error: true`). The workflow states its purpose at `:253-254`:

```
# The advisory Windows job detects path, temporary-directory, Git, and file-lock regressions.
# Windows is not a supported gate target, so failures remain visible without blocking merges.
```

The job is currently red at a scale that defeats that purpose.

## Measurement

Run 35250748887, `workflow_dispatch` on merged ref `4f12815e9a0b0cee5ded72d73e22256115e10c87`:

```
1626 failed, 16984 passed, 281 skipped, 1683 warnings, 1382 errors in 5514.06s (1:31:54)
```

Error-signature census across the run:

| Count | Signature |
|---:|---|
| 2722 | `PermissionError` |
| 136 | `ModuleNotFoundError` |
| 63 | `FileNotFoundError [WinError]` |
| 34 | `OSError` |
| 21 | `FileNotFoundError('shell not found: ...')` |
| 19 | `OSError [WinError]` |
| 16 | `AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute` |
| 10 | `AttributeError: module 'signal' has no attribute` |
| 4 | `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'` |
| 4 | `AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute` |

## The dominant class: Windows path length

The most frequently visible failure in the `FAILED` lines is `MAX_PATH` exhaustion during gate-snapshot materialisation:

```
rebar._snapshot.git_fetch.SnapshotError: git checkout-index for 2c684ee31a74 failed:
error: unable to create file C:\Users\runneradmin\AppData\Local\Temp\pytest-of-runneradmin\
pytest-1\popen-gw3\gate-store\rebar-gate-snapshots\tmp\
tickets-2c684ee31a74-57739aaf299d4a5ca43572977cd0316c\.tickets-tracker\4805-7680-90b5-4fef\
1789665984171900001-4960ae39-c6d4-42a1-9f62-0ae54f3992a1-CREATE.json: Filename too long
```

The path is built from several nested components that each contribute length: the pytest tmp root, the per-worker xdist directory (`popen-gw3`), the gate-store root, a snapshot directory carrying a full 32-character hex suffix, the tracker directory, a four-quad ticket id directory, and finally an event filename combining a nanosecond timestamp with a full UUID. Affected modules observed include `tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_ref_coherence.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_sign_transaction_lifecycle.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_gate_ticket_snapshot.py`, and `tests/interfaces/store/test_snapshot_environments.py`.

Two candidate remedies exist and they are not equivalent: enabling long-path support on the runner and in Git (`core.longpaths`), versus shortening the constructed path. The former is an environment change that may not hold for downstream consumers on Windows; the latter changes behaviour that POSIX platforms also exercise. That tradeoff needs deciding rather than assuming.

## Not all of it is path length

At least four further classes are present and need separating before any fix:

1. `PermissionError` at high volume — likely Windows file-locking semantics where a handle is still open when a test tries to delete or replace a file. This is exactly the "temporary-directory and file-lock regression" the job exists to detect.
2. `shell not found` — tests assuming a POSIX shell is available.
3. `AttributeError: module 'signal' has no attribute ...` — POSIX-only signal names.
4. Residual `fcntl` imports (4 occurrences, outside the module already fixed under `visionary-geologic-harrier`).

## Why this matters even though the job does not gate

An advisory job exists to make regressions visible. At 1626 failures it cannot do that: a genuine new Windows regression is indistinguishable from the standing noise, so the signal is already lost. This is the same failure mode recorded in `enviable-beloved-buffalo` (dead metrics leaving alarms unfalsifiable) and `catty-giddied-hedgehog` (an alarm latched for days) — a monitoring surface that cannot change state carries no information.

A decision is therefore required up front, and it is a scoping decision rather than a technical one: either Windows is worth supporting to the point where this job can be read, or the job should be reduced to the subset that is genuinely maintained so that subset can be held green. Filing at P3 because Windows is explicitly not a gate target; the priority should be revisited once the scoping decision is made.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The 1626 failures and 1382 errors are classified into named defect classes with a count per class, so the work can be scoped and split.
- [ ] The `MAX_PATH` remedy is chosen explicitly between runner/Git long-path support and path shortening, with the tradeoff for downstream Windows consumers recorded.
- [ ] The `PermissionError` population is diagnosed rather than assumed — confirmed as file-handle lifetime, or identified as something else.
- [ ] A scoping decision is recorded: either Windows is supported to a readable-green standard, or the advisory job is narrowed to a maintained subset that is held green.
- [ ] After the change, `sweep (windows)` is in a state where a NEW regression would be visible — either green, or red with a known and enumerated baseline that CI compares against.
compiled_state.title: Advisory sweep (windows) is red at a scale that destroys its signal: 1626 failures across five defect classes
